create.name: Atlanta Soto Zen Center
create.bio:
Atlanta Soto Zen Center is a lay Zen community on Zonolite Place in north-east Atlanta, near the Emory University campus. It was formed in the 1970s under Zenkai Taiun Michael Elliston, an artist and designer from Illinois who had trained in Chicago in the 1960s with Soyu Matsuoka, one of the first Japanese Soto priests to settle in the United States; the centre also traces its roots to Shohaku Okumura. Elliston remains its abbot and also heads the Silent Thunder Order, the centre's network of affiliated sitting groups in Georgia, Tennessee, Alabama, Kansas and beyond.

The centre is run by and for householders rather than monks. Zazen is held mornings and evenings through the week, in person and, where possible, online, and newcomers are taught the basics of posture, breath and attention at a regular Wednesday evening workshop. Monthly all-day sittings, occasional week-long sesshin, a monthly seminar with the abbot and discussion groups fill out the calendar, and there is a lending library and a meditation programme for people in Georgia's prisons. Services cost nothing and run on donations. A residency is open to committed students, and talks are shared through a podcast and a YouTube channel.

courses.title: Newcomers Workshop: Introduction to Zen Meditation
courses.description: Meditation instruction for beginners on the first and third Wednesday of the month at 7 pm, covering posture, breath and attention, with time to ask questions. Experienced sitters may join any regular service.
courses.price: There is no cost for our services (dana welcome)

courses.title: Roshi Seminar 2026: Sharpening the Razorblade of Zen
courses.description: A Saturday morning seminar with the abbot on the fourth Saturday of each month, working through his book The Razorblade of Zen with commentary and an open question-and-answer dialogue.

courses.title: Residential Practice
courses.description: A residency for committed Zen students at the centre, who join the regular Sunday and weekday sittings and may attend all events. Short stays are also offered; longer residencies follow a 90-day agreement arranged with the abbot.
courses.price: Short term residency available for $50 per night

free_resources.title: Practicing Zen At Home
free_resources.description: Materials for a daily home practice: guided audio on posture, breath and attention at beginner and intermediate level, a home liturgy manual, the service chant book and illustrated booklets on sitting, walking and chair meditation. A small donation is suggested.

free_resources.title: UnMind podcast
free_resources.description: A podcast of teachings and music from the abbot, Zenkai Taiun Michael Elliston, available by RSS and on the main podcast apps.
